events.title: Bronze Age Civilization
events.description: Early Bronze Age civilizations emerged on Armenian Plateau. Archaeological discoveries show advanced metallurgy, agriculture and trade. This region was one of important centers of early human civilization.

events.title: Kingdom of Urartu
events.description: Kingdom of Urartu established in Armenian Highland, capital Tushpa (modern Van). Urartu competed with Assyria for control of eastern Anatolia, developing advanced irrigation systems and fortresses. Urartian culture laid foundation for later Armenian civilization.

events.title: Persian Rule and Armenian Formation
events.description: Urartu conquered by Medes and Persians. Armenians as distinct people formed during this period, merging local and Indo-European migrants. Under Persian Achaemenid Empire, Armenia existed as satrapy.

events.title: Alexander's Conquest
events.description: Alexander the Great conquered Persian Empire, Armenia entered Hellenistic era. After Seleucid rule, Armenian local governors gradually became independent.

events.title: Rise of Artaxiad Dynasty
events.description: Artaxes I established Artaxiad Dynasty, unifying Armenian regions. He founded capital Artashat, developed administrative and military systems, laying foundation for Kingdom of Greater Armenia.

events.title: Kingdom of Greater Armenia
events.description: Under Tigranes II (Tigranes the Great, 95-55 BCE), Armenia reached zenith, territory extending from Caspian Sea to Mediterranean, becoming one of era's most powerful states. Tigranes conquered Syria and Lebanon, capital Tigranocerta had hundreds of thousands inhabitants. But conflict with Rome led to empire's decline.

events.title: Arsacid Dynasty
events.description: Persian-backed Arsacid Dynasty ruled Armenia, becoming buffer state between Rome and Persia. Armenia skillfully maneuvered between two empires, maintaining relative independence.

events.title: Conversion to Christianity
events.description: Under St. Gregory the Illuminator's preaching, King Tiridates III declared Armenia's conversion to Christianity, becoming world's first official Christian state (before Roman Empire). Christianity became core of Armenian identity, continuing to this day.

events.title: Creation of Armenian Alphabet
events.description: Monk-scholar Mesrop Mashtots created Armenian alphabet with 36 letters (later increased to 39). Alphabet creation preserved Armenian language and culture, promoting literature and religious text translation. Bible was translated into Armenian, called 'Queen of Translations.'

events.title: End of Armenian Kingdom
events.description: Persian Sassanid Dynasty deposed last Armenian king, ending Arsacid Dynasty. Armenia was divided into Persian and Byzantine spheres of influence, entering centuries of foreign rule.

events.title: Battle of Avarayr
events.description: Armenia under Vardan Mamikonian resisted Persian Sassanid dynasty, defending Christian faith against Zoroastrianism. Though defeated, Persians eventually allowed Armenians religious freedom. This battle became symbol of Armenian resistance and faith.

events.title: Armenian Golden Age Literature
events.description: Armenia experienced cultural and literary flourishing. Historians like Movses Khorenatsi wrote 'History of Armenia', preserving national history and legends. Monasteries became centers of learning and culture.

events.title: Arab Conquest
events.description: Arab Muslims conquered Armenia, establishing emirate rule. Armenians were allowed to maintain Christian faith but had to pay heavy taxes. Some Armenian nobles cooperated with Arabs to retain power.

events.title: Bagratid Dynasty
events.description: After Arab Caliphate decline, Bagratid dynasty established independent Armenian kingdom in Ani. Ani became 'city of thousand churches,' population reached 100,000, important Silk Road trade center. This was Armenia's medieval golden age.

events.title: Byzantine Annexation of Ani
events.description: Byzantine Empire annexed Ani and Bagratid kingdom, weakening Armenian defenses. Subsequently Seljuk Turks invaded, Armenia suffered devastating blow. Many Armenians migrated west and south.

events.title: Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia
events.description: Armenians fleeing Seljuks established Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia on eastern Mediterranean coast (modern southern Turkey). This 'Little Armenia' allied with Crusaders, becoming East-West trade hub. But eventually conquered by Mamluks.

events.title: Mongol and Turkmen Rule
events.description: After Cilician Kingdom fell, Armenia suffered successive invasions by Mongols, Timurids, and Turkmen tribes. Armenian lands were divided among various Muslim dynasties. This was darkest period in Armenian history.

events.title: Great Diaspora and Julfa
events.description: Persian Shah Abbas I forcibly relocated tens of thousands of Armenians from Julfa to Isfahan, creating New Julfa. This became prosperous Armenian merchant community, but homeland was devastated. Armenian diaspora expanded globally.

events.title: Armenian National Revival Movement
events.description: Armenian intellectuals in Russian and Ottoman territories promoted national consciousness. Literature, press, and education flourished. Armenians sought autonomy and reforms but faced opposition from Ottoman Empire.

events.title: Hamidian Massacres
events.description: Under Sultan Abdul Hamid II, Ottoman Empire massacred 100,000-300,000 Armenians. This was prelude to later genocide. International outcry occurred but no effective intervention.

events.title: Russian Conquest of Eastern Armenia
events.description: After Russo-Turkish and Russo-Persian wars, Russia seized Eastern Armenia (Yerevan and Karabakh) from Persia and Ottomans. Armenia divided into Russian-ruled east and Ottoman-ruled west. Under Russian rule, Armenia experienced modernization and national awakening.

events.title: Turkish-Armenian War
events.description: Turkish nationalist forces attacked First Republic, seizing western Armenian territories. Soviet Red Army then invaded from east. Armenia lost independence, forced to become Soviet republic.

events.title: Armenian Genocide
events.description: During WWI, Young Turk government systematically eliminated Ottoman Armenians. About 1.5 million Armenians killed or died in death marches and concentration camps. Intellectuals, clergy and community leaders first arrested and executed. Women and children driven to Syrian desert, hundreds of thousands starved or killed. This was 20th century's first genocide, but Turkey still refuses recognition.

events.title: First Republic of Armenia
events.description: After Russian Revolution and Ottoman Empire collapse, Armenia declared independence, establishing Democratic Republic of Armenia. Capital Yerevan received hundreds of thousands genocide survivors. But new state faced Turkish invasion, disease, famine and refugee crisis.

events.title: Great Purge
events.description: Stalin's Great Purge struck Armenia. Thousands of intellectuals, party officials, and military officers were executed or sent to gulags. Armenian cultural and political elite was decimated.

events.title: Turkish-Armenian War
events.description: Kemalist Turkish army invaded Armenia, occupying western territories including Kars. Armenia forced to sign humiliating Treaty of Alexandropol, ceding vast territory.

events.title: Genocide 50th Anniversary Commemoration
events.description: On genocide's 50th anniversary, Armenians held unprecedented mass demonstrations in Yerevan demanding recognition. This broke Soviet taboo. Genocide Memorial was built. Armenian national consciousness strengthened.

events.title: Karabakh Movement
events.description: Nagorno-Karabakh (Armenian-majority region in Azerbaijan) voted to join Armenia. This triggered mass demonstrations in Yerevan and ethnic conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan. This was major catalyst for Soviet collapse.

events.title: Sovietization
events.description: Red Army invaded, First Republic of Armenia overthrown, Soviet regime established. Armenia became part of Transcaucasian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (with Georgia and Azerbaijan), 1936 became independent Soviet republic.

events.title: Soviet Rule
events.description: During 70 years Soviet rule, Armenia experienced industrialization, collectivization and cultural suppression. Stalin-era Great Purge and repressions. But Soviets also brought modernization, education and stability. Armenia developed strong scientific and industrial base. Genocide memory suppressed but not forgotten.

events.title: Nagorno-Karabakh Conflict Begins
events.description: Nagorno-Karabakh (predominantly Armenian) demanded transfer from Azerbaijan to Armenia. Pogroms against Armenians occurred in Sumgait, Baku. Conflict quickly escalated to war, accelerating Soviet collapse.

events.title: Spitak Earthquake
events.description: 7.0 magnitude earthquake struck northern Armenia, Spitak and Leninakan (Gyumri) almost completely destroyed, about 25,000 killed, 500,000 homeless. Gorbachev interrupted US visit to return. Earthquake exacerbated Armenia's difficulties.

events.title: Armenian Independence
events.description: After Soviet collapse, Armenia voted for independence, Levon Ter-Petrosyan elected first president. Armenia regained independence but faced war with Azerbaijan, economic collapse and Turkey-Azerbaijan blockade.

events.title: First Nagorno-Karabakh War
events.description: Armenia and Azerbaijan fought full war over Nagorno-Karabakh. Armenian forces victorious, controlling Karabakh and 7 surrounding Azerbaijani regions. About 30,000 killed, over 1 million displaced (both sides). 1994 ceasefire but no peace treaty, conflict frozen.

events.title: Economic Crisis and Blockade
events.description: Post-independence Armenia experienced severe economic crisis. Turkey and Azerbaijan blockaded borders. Energy shortage, winter only few hours electricity and heating. Economic collapse, mass emigration (about 1 million people). But Armenia persisted, diaspora provided crucial aid.

events.title: Kocharyan Presidency
events.description: Robert Kocharyan (former Karabakh leader) served as president. Economy began recovering, but corruption and authoritarianism intensified. Kocharyan hardline on Karabakh issue, refusing compromise.

events.title: Sargsyan Rule
events.description: Serzh Sargsyan served as president for 10 years. Economic growth but inequality worsened. Corruption rampant, ruling elite monopolized economy. 2015 constitutional reform changed from presidential to parliamentary system, viewed as Sargsyan's way to extend power.

events.title: Four-Day War
events.description: Azerbaijan launched large-scale offensive in Karabakh, breaking defensive lines. Four days intense fighting caused hundreds deaths, Azerbaijan seized some territory. This was most serious combat since 1994 ceasefire, showing conflict could reignite anytime.

events.title: Velvet Revolution
events.description: Sargsyan's attempt to continue power by switching from president to PM triggered mass protests. Nikol Pashinyan led nonviolent civil disobedience, hundreds of thousands took to streets. Sargsyan forced to resign, Pashinyan elected PM. This 'Velvet Revolution' became example of democratic victory.

events.title: Pashinyan Reforms
events.description: Pashinyan promised anti-corruption, rule of law and democratic reforms. Arrested former officials, reformed judiciary. But reforms faced resistance, old elites resisted. Pashinyan sought compromise on Karabakh issue, triggering hardliner criticism.

events.title: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
events.description: Azerbaijan launched full offensive on Karabakh with Turkish support. Azerbaijan used Israeli and Turkish drones, dominating air. Armenian forces retreated, thousands died. After 44-day war, Russia brokered ceasefire. Armenia forced to surrender vast territory, Russian peacekeepers deployed.

events.title: Catastrophic Defeat and Political Crisis
events.description: Ceasefire agreement triggered Armenian anger and trauma. Pashinyan accused of treason, opposition demanded resignation, military demanded he step down. Armenia experienced profound political crisis and identity crisis. Thousands soldiers killed, tens of thousands refugees evacuated from Karabakh.

events.title: Elections and Pashinyan Re-elected
events.description: Pashinyan called snap parliamentary elections seeking legitimacy. Despite defeat, his party won, reflecting people's rejection of old elites. But Armenia remained deeply divided, future uncertain.

events.title: Continued Azerbaijani Aggression
events.description: Azerbaijan continued encroaching on Armenian territory, ignoring ceasefire. September 2022 Azerbaijan attacked Armenian mainland, causing hundreds deaths. Russia (traditional ally) failed to effectively protect Armenia, focused on Ukraine war.

events.title: Fall of Karabakh and Exodus
events.description: Azerbaijan blockaded Lachin corridor (only road connecting Armenia and Karabakh) for months, causing humanitarian crisis. September 2023 Azerbaijan launched 24-hour blitzkrieg, Karabakh surrendered. Almost all 120,000 Armenians fled to Armenia, Armenian presence in Karabakh ended. This was one of Armenia's greatest modern disasters.

events.title: Survival and Adaptation
events.description: Armenia faces existential crisis: lost Karabakh, territorial integrity threatened, Russian ally unreliable, hostile to Turkey and Azerbaijan. Pashinyan seeks Western alignment, strengthening relations with US and EU. Armenia attempts normalization with Turkey and peace with Azerbaijan, but prospects unclear. Internally divided politically, economic difficulties, 120,000 Karabakh refugees need resettlement. But Armenian people show sumud (steadfastness) tradition, adapting to new reality. Armenia's future depends on finding security and prosperity path in hostile region while maintaining unique identity and culture. From ancient kingdoms to genocide survivors to modern democracy, Armenia's story is epic of resilience, faith and survival.

events.title: 選舉與帕希尼揚連任
events.description: 帕希尼揚提前舉行議會選舉以尋求合法性。儘管戰敗，他的政黨仍獲勝，反映人民對舊精英的拒絕。但亞美尼亞仍深度分裂，未來不確定。...

events.description: 阿塞拜疆繼續侵占亞美尼亞領土，無視停火。2022年9月阿塞拜疆攻擊亞美尼亞本土，造成數百人死亡。俄羅斯（傳統盟友）未能有效保護亞美尼亞，專注於烏克蘭戰爭。...
